purpose: Pin the real asyncdb distribution used as the load-bearing consumer for strict datamodel compatibility, so no test can run against a guessed or faked API.

artifact.name: asyncdb
artifact.author: Jesus Lara <jesuslara@phenobarbital.info>
artifact.company_relevance: Same author and maintainer as python-datamodel; asyncdb is the Navigator data-access layer and declares python-datamodel>=0.10.21, which is exactly the engineering reference version this feature is measured against. It is therefore the real downstream consumer named in spec section 8, not a proxy.

verified_adapter_api.note: Every entry below was verified by import and call against the installed artifact. Nothing here was inferred from a filename or a docstring.

datamodel_surface_consumed_by_asyncdb.note: asyncdb/models/model.py imports these directly. They are a wider public surface than BaseModel alone, and a break in any of them breaks the consumer.
datamodel_surface_consumed_by_asyncdb.mutation: asyncdb sets DB_TYPES[numpy.int64] = 'bigint' at import time, so importing asyncdb mutates a datamodel module-level dict.

offline_methods_exercised.constructor: Model(**row) - hydration, coercion, defaults, required/null, aliases, nested relations
offline_methods_exercised.Model.model: classmethod(dialect='sql') -> str; renders DDL via cls.columns(), field.db_type(), field.required(), field.primary_key
offline_methods_exercised.columns: cls.columns(cls) -> mapping of column name to Field
offline_methods_exercised.set_connection: stores an object on Meta.connection; exercised with an inert stub, no I/O

excluded_methods.reason: All are async and require a live database connection. The task forbids production database access, so they are out of scope and are NOT claimed as verified.
excluded_methods.get_connection: Not called: it imports asyncdb.drivers.<driver> and constructs a real client.

environments.note: asyncdb is installed with --no-deps into each environment's own venv so that each one binds its own datamodel build. Installing with dependencies would pull python-datamodel from PyPI and silently shadow the build under test.

external_prerequisites_pending.note: Recorded explicitly rather than silently omitted, per the task's requirement that genuine remaining external prerequisites be stated.
items: No company-internal asyncdb fork or private index was provided. This manifest pins the public PyPI distribution by the same author. If a private Navigator build diverges from 2.16.0, that build must be re-pinned here and the differential re-run before consumer compatibility can be claimed for it.

Live database driver integration (postgres/mysql/redis backends) is NOT covered: it requires service credentials that this task is not authorized to use. Driver-level compatibility therefore remains evidence-pending.
